DOC-FOUNDATION.title: Documentation responsibility/provenance foundation
DOC-FOUNDATION.strongest_evidence_against: Evidence that separating current state, historical index and subsystem contracts destroys required provenance, creates competing current sources of truth, or makes current project status harder to reconstruct.
DOC-FOUNDATION.contrary_found: Final PR #77 links PROJECT_HISTORY from both PROJECT_STATE and README, explicitly keeps Git/PRs primary historical evidence, and leaves permanent contracts in their subsystem documents. The audit itself could reconstruct the relevant chains from primary evidence.
DOC-FOUNDATION.effect: Intentional documentation foundation; this does not grant authority to the retrospective conclusions stored in the index.

DOC-ALTERNATIVE.title: Documentation organization/planning alternative
DOC-ALTERNATIVE.strongest_evidence_against: Evidence that removing chronology from PROJECT_STATE, shortening the nearest route, or adding history links hides a required current constraint or contradicts an accepted stage boundary.
DOC-ALTERNATIVE.contrary_found: The structural choices are compatible with the accepted product-first Stage 5/Stage 6 split. Specific omitted current defects are classified separately rather than used to condemn the organization model itself.

DEF-HISTORY-LOSS.title: Intermediate history-loss defect
DEF-HISTORY-LOSS.strongest_evidence_against: Evidence that all removed PROJECT_STATE provenance already had a durable, linked historical owner before bec8226 landed.
DEF-HISTORY-LOSS.contrary_found: bec8226 removed the accumulated chronology before PROJECT_HISTORY existed; af7825b and later link commits were required afterward to restore an accessible history path.
DEF-HISTORY-LOSS.effect: Real historical documentation defect inside PR #77, fixed before merge.

DEF-PR40-SUMMARY.title: Overbroad PR #40 retrospective label
DEF-PR40-SUMMARY.strongest_evidence_against: A reading in which the summary's `stale-pack cleanup, later recognized regression` refers only to the independently proven zero-stale gate and not to the mixed PR #40 cleanup/canary changes as a whole.
DEF-PR40-SUMMARY.contrary_found: The accepted stale-chain result classifies EX40-02 as the dumb correction but EX40-01 and EX40-03 as acceptable alternatives and keeps EX77-29/30 evidence-limited. The high-level PROJECT_HISTORY bullet collapses those mixed outcomes into one regression label.
DEF-PR40-SUMMARY.effect: Real current documentation overstatement. This does not reopen the already accepted stale-chain IDs.

DEF-AUTHZ-PROVENANCE.title: Incorrect PR #61 causal attribution
DEF-AUTHZ-PROVENANCE.strongest_evidence_against: Evidence that broad authorization failure handling first appeared only in review-follow-up commits.
DEF-AUTHZ-PROVENANCE.contrary_found: The first PR #61 implementation already mapped arbitrary resolver failures to controlled unavailability in protected paths; later review follow-ups broadened optional-presentation suppression. Commit 9c1fa30 corrected this exact provenance.
DEF-AUTHZ-PROVENANCE.effect: Real historical documentation defect, corrected before PR #77 merge.

DEF-HISTORY-OMISSION.title: PROJECT_HISTORY omission of an accepted current defect
DEF-HISTORY-OMISSION.strongest_evidence_against: Evidence that the omitted PR review was resolved by later code, was only a speculative review concern, or was outside the history file's stated purpose.
DEF-HISTORY-OMISSION.contrary_found: Accepted DL-CLASSIFY-007 independently confirms both the #72 A→B→A starvation path and #75 durable v1→v2 refresh gap as current defects. PROJECT_HISTORY says it indexes significant regressions and known historical problems still unfixed, yet neither review is indexed.
DEF-HISTORY-OMISSION.effect: Real current documentation-completeness defect; it does not independently prove or enlarge the underlying runtime defect.

DEF-STATE-OMISSION.title: PROJECT_STATE omission of an accepted current constraint
DEF-STATE-OMISSION.strongest_evidence_against: Evidence that the omitted review does not describe current behavior, was fixed before main, or is irrelevant to PROJECT_STATE's stated role of recording known current constraints.
DEF-STATE-OMISSION.contrary_found: Accepted DL-CLASSIFY-007 confirms both defects remain in current main. Final PROJECT_STATE describes Stage 5A capabilities and known current limitations but names only the stale-pack regression, omitting these two confirmed Stage 5A constraints.
DEF-STATE-OMISSION.effect: Real current documentation-state omission; no runtime conclusion is inferred beyond the already accepted underlying findings.

FIX-CI.title: Factual CI/state correction
FIX-CI.strongest_evidence_against: Evidence that CI #202/code head was already the final PR #76 acceptance evidence or that CI #203/final head did not exist.
FIX-CI.contrary_found: Accepted PR #76 extraction/classification records final CI #203 on final head; 089f11c changes the stale code-head reference to that final evidence.
FIX-CI.effect: Justified documentation correction of a factual state defect.

FIX-STAGE.title: Stage 5 local/CI versus Stage 6 external state correction
FIX-STAGE.strongest_evidence_against: Evidence that concrete provider-adapter implementation was external-only Stage 6 work, or that real Queue/provider acceptance was required to complete ordinary Stage 5 local/CI work.
FIX-STAGE.contrary_found: The accepted PR #50 boundary and current ROADMAP separate local/CI Stage 5 implementation from Stage 6 external acceptance; 8f75a43 corrects the rebuilt state to keep the concrete adapter local while deferring real bindings/credentials/smoke.
FIX-STAGE.effect: Justified correction of intermediate PROJECT_STATE wording/route.

FIX-HISTORY.title: Restoration of lost or omitted significant history
FIX-HISTORY.strongest_evidence_against: Evidence that the restored episode was factually unsupported, trivial to the history file's stated purpose, or already indexed elsewhere.
FIX-HISTORY.contrary_found: The restored history is independently present in Git/accepted audit findings: PR #77's own history-loss episode, PR #61 provenance split, and the #69/#71 missing-return regressions are all corroborated by commits/reviews.
FIX-HISTORY.effect: Justified documentation correction; it does not make the retrospective file authority for the underlying event.

INSUF-USER-REVIEW.title: Uncorroborated user-review attribution
INSUF-USER-REVIEW.strongest_evidence_against: A preserved user message, task artifact, or PR discussion showing that the user specifically detected the history-loss episode before merge.
INSUF-USER-REVIEW.contrary_found: Git proves the history loss and its later correction, but the available PR #77 GitHub discussion contains only the Codex usage-limit bot message. The later PROJECT_HISTORY assertion cannot prove its own `user review` attribution.
INSUF-USER-REVIEW.effect: Insufficient evidence for who detected the defect; the defect and correction themselves remain independently supported.
